To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) 23% of participants who had no sex after they knew their seropositive status started to have sex again after starting ART, 2) 56% of participants had sex in the last 6 months, and 3) 26.5-28.4% of the participants had sex with nonregular partners.
23% of HIV-infected patients who had no sexual contact after they knew their status started to have sex again after ART.

the prevalence of unprotected sex in HIV-infected patients who had received antiretrovial therapy for at least 6 months in Thailand was 56%, and there was a significant difference in the number of those who had sex before and after starting antiretrovirus therapy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
sexual behavior and the use of condoms in the context of antiretrovirals in Thailand.
the risk behaviors of the Thai HIV-infected population in the ART era.
the sexual behaviors of HIV-infected persons receiving ART.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
sexual behavior of HIV-infected individuals is still a major problem in the era of ART.
sexual behavior is not a risk factor for the development of drug-resistant HIV strains in the ART era in Thailand, but it may be a risk factor for other sexually transmitted diseases.
sexual risk behavior among patients receiving ART in this study was not associated with CD4 counts, but was associated with the status of their regular partner.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the sexual risk behavior of HIV-infected patients in Thailand has increased in the era of ART, and the inconsistent condom use among HIV-infected females is higher than that among males.
sexual behavior of HIV infected people on antiretrovial therapy is increasing.
sexual behaviors during antireviral therapy among patients with HIV infection in the Thai National Antiretrovirals Program are still risky.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we need to continue to provide risk-reduction counseling for people who are HIV-infected and on ART.
we found that people who were receiving antiretrovirus therapy were having unprotected sex with their partners.
we need to do more to help people living with HIV to protect their health, and to help them to protect their sexual partners.
